title: Month and Year of Manufacture/Packing Present
description: Detect whether the month and year of manufacture, pre-packing, or import is declared on the package. This check identifies the presence of a date declaration. It does not verify the date format against the applicable law for the specific product category.
amendment_status: Amendments 2012–2026 not text-verified. This rule is based solely on the original 2011 text.
applicable_scope: All pre-packaged commodities intended for retail sale, excluding: packages >25kg/25L (Rule 3(a)), industrial/institutional consumers (Rule 3(b)). Multiple exemptions apply — see limitations.
conditions: Not required for: bidis, incense sticks (Rule 6(1)(A)(i))
Not required for: domestic LPG cylinders of 14.2kg or 5kg (Rule 6(1)(A)(ii))
Food articles: follow Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 provisions (Rule 6(1)(d) first proviso)
Seeds: follow Seeds Act, 1966 provisions (Rule 6(1)(d) second proviso)
Cosmetics: follow Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 provisions (Rule 6(1)(d) third proviso)

detection_method.description: OCR extracts all text. The system searches for date-like patterns: month names/abbreviations with year, or numeric month/year formats, near date-related keywords.

validation_logic.pass_criteria: A month+year combination is found in the OCR text, either as a standalone date or near a date-related keyword.

evaluate.action: If date_matches contains month+year → DETECTED. If date_matches contains partial date (year only or month only) → UNCERTAIN. If keyword_matches found but no date → UNCERTAIN. If neither found → NOT_DETECTED.

observable_evidence.description: What the software can observe: a text string containing a month name/abbreviation and a year (e.g., 'March 2024', '03/2024', 'Mfg: Jan 2025'), or a date-related keyword followed by a date pattern.
examples: Text 'Batch: AB123' found but no date pattern

status_values.DETECTED: A month+year date pattern was found on the label.
status_values.NOT_DETECTED: No date pattern or date-related keyword was found.
status_values.UNCERTAIN: A partial date (year only, month only) or a date keyword without an associated date was found.
status_values.NOT_APPLICABLE: Product is exempt (bidis, incense sticks, LPG, food, cosmetics, seeds). Requires manual classification.

cannot_conclude: Whether the date format satisfies the LMPC requirement for this specific product category
Whether a food product's 'Best before' / 'Use by' date satisfies the Rule 6(1)(d) requirement
Whether the date follows the allowance for rubber stamp usage (withdrawn by GSR 748(E) 2012)
Whether the packaging material reuse provision (Rule 6(1)(B)) applies
notes: Rule 6(1)(d): 'The month and year in which the commodity is manufactured or pre-packed or imported shall be mentioned in the package.'
Rule 6(1)(d) Explanation I: 'The month and the year in which commodity is pre-packed may be expressed either in words, or by numerals indicating the month and the year, or by both.'
Rule 6(1)(B): Packaging material from a previous month may be used for the next succeeding month only.
The system detects presence of a date pattern. Format compliance is reported as an observation only.
Food products commonly use 'Best before' or 'Use by' dates which may or may not satisfy Rule 6(1)(d). The system notes this ambiguity.
limitations: Based on original 2011 text only. Amendments may have modified date format requirements.
Multiple product-category exemptions mean the system may flag products that are legally exempt.
OCR may misread date characters (e.g., '0' as 'O', '1' as 'l').
Some products use batch codes or lot numbers instead of explicit dates — the system cannot interpret these.
The 'when packed' provision (Third Schedule) may affect date interpretation for certain commodities.
